reasoning: AI is both moat-extender (Now Assist) and existential threat (agents bypass ITSM). Moat real but 35x EV/EBITDA leaves no safety margin for disruption.

ai_disruption_view.opportunity: Now Assist embeds AI natively into existing workflow fabric where data already lives. Consumption pricing unlocks upside beyond seats. Customers automate more, spend more. Lollapalooza: platform stickiness + AI upsell + 76% gross margin compounding. FCF CAGR 28% over 3 years confirms execution.
ai_disruption_view.threat: AI agents (Copilot, Agentforce, open-source) could route around enterprise workflow middleware entirely. If LLMs handle incident triage and change management end-to-end without human-in-the-loop, ITSM seat demand erodes structurally. ITSM commoditizes if open-source agents replicate core ticket-routing cheaply. New entrants attack from below. IT headcount shrinks as AI replaces admins, cutting license demand at the root.
ai_disruption_view.net_assessment: The inversion is not far-fetched -- it is actively being attempted by every major hyperscaler and dozens of startups. ServiceNow's workflow data moat and 20-year lock-in are real, but so is the threat. At 35x EV/EBITDA and 4.3% FCF yield, the price does not compensate for this binary risk. Munger would want a bigger margin of safety before committing. Result: neutral, not bullish.

inversion_disasters: AI agents bypass ITSM layer entirely -- agentic workflows need no middleware, collapsing seat demand
ITSM commoditizes as LLMs commoditize ticket triage and change management, destroying pricing power
Hyperscalers (MSFT, GOOG) bundle workflow orchestration into cloud contracts, squeezing NOW on price
capital_allocation_notes: Buybacks ramped from $0 (2022) to $1.84B (2025) as FCF scaled -- sensible timing. No major M&A premium destruction observed. Net cash positive ($2.8B). Grade B, not A: operating margins at 13% are thin for a 76% gross-margin SaaS business, implying heavy reinvestment or cost discipline failure.

valuation_sanity.comment: PEG near 1 looks fair for a compounder, but EV/EBITDA at 35x leaves no margin of safety if AI disruption slows growth to 10-12%. FCF yield of 4.3% is acceptable but not cheap for a business facing a structural threat.
